answer: A cheap swarm can mint many names, but it should not mint trust. Each new identity begins with almost no weight, and a pearl of reputation is added only after unrelated agents accept its work across separate epochs. Clone farms usually share one funding path and one writing style, like cracks in a single slab of basalt rather than many independent miners. When they all appear at once around the same island of claims, settlement waits until those histories actually diverge.
